title: A differential derivation of the Obara-Saika relation for Gaussian electron repulsion integrals
authors: Charles C. Forgy, David A. Mazziotti
abstract: The Obara-Saika (OS) method is one of the most widely used techniques in quantum chemistry for evaluating electron repulsion integrals (ERIs) via a set of recurrence relations that build higher angular momentum integrals from lower-order ones. The original derivation by Obara and Saika proceeded by directly relating integrals of differing angular momentum. In this work, we present a compact novel derivation of the OS vertical recurrence relation based solely on differential relations between Gaussian basis functions, expanding on a method suggested in earlier work. By explicitly deriving the required derivative expressions we identify all non-zero primitive terms contributing to the full ERI to develop a hierarchical formulation of the OS recursion relations. This approach has pedagogical value as a rigorous and self-contained derivation. Additionally, the resulting organization exposes independent primitive derivative quantities and may be useful for code generation and parallel implementations on modern GPU architectures.
summary: This paper presents a novel, purely differential derivation of the Obara-Saika recurrence relation used to calculate electron repulsion integrals (ERIs) in quantum chemistry. By deriving these relations solely from the derivatives of Gaussian basis functions, the authors provide a self-contained and pedagogically valuable method. This new formulation is designed to expose independent primitive derivative terms, making the calculation highly suitable for modern parallel hardware like GPUs.
main_problem: The core problem is developing a novel, rigorous derivation for calculating complex two-electron repulsion integrals (ERIs) required in quantum chemistry calculations.
main_result: The authors successfully derive the Obara-Saika recurrence relation using only differential relations between Gaussian basis functions, yielding a hierarchical formulation of the integral calculation.
method: The method involves applying repeated differentiation operators ($\partial/\partial A_i$) to the ERI expressions and utilizing established mathematical identities (like Lemma 1) to build up higher-order integrals from lower ones.
model_or_system: The calculations are performed for electronic structure problems using Gaussian basis sets, specifically focusing on two-center four-orbital electron repulsion integrals ($\langle ss|ss angle$, etc.).
key_observables: Electron Repulsion Integrals (ERIs), the Obara-Saika recurrence relation (OS-VRR), and independent primitive derivative quantities.
important_parameters: Gaussian coefficients, nuclear coordinates ($A, B, C, D$), and angular momentum indices.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on the mathematical validity of applying differential operators to Gaussian basis functions; numerical instability is noted as a practical limitation when using recursion for Boys functions.
figures_summary: Not specified (Notes focus heavily on equations and derivations rather than figure descriptions).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the need for ERI calculation, introducing the differential approach based on Gaussian derivatives, deriving recurrence relations step-by-step using operators, and finally comparing the resulting relation to the established OS method.
why_interesting: While focused on quantum chemistry integrals rather than AMO systems, the rigorous development of a computationally efficient, parallelizable mathematical framework for calculating complex multi-electron interactions is highly relevant to any field involving many-body electronic structure calculations.
